blocks.raw: <Tip>_Soft_ = stiffness (S.S. = Same Sound). _Weak_ = strength (starts with W). Soft < 70%; Weak < 80%. Remember: 70 (soft) comes before 80 (weak) numerically and alphabetically (Soft, Weak).</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Treating soft and weak as synonyms. They are distinct: soft = stiffness; weak = strength. Different definitions, different thresholds (70% vs. 80%).","Using 80% for soft story threshold. Soft story threshold is 70% of story above (stiffness). Weak story is 80% (strength).","Confusing story drift (displacement) with soft/weak (stiffness/strength). Drift is the lateral movement; soft/weak are structural deficiencies that can cause excessive drift.","Thinking soft/weak stories only matter for tall buildings. Any building with a stiffness or strength discontinuity (e.g., ground floor retail below office) is subject to the check.","Ignoring the story-pair nature of the check. A soft story is 70% of the story ABOVE, not an absolute value. Compare each story to its upper neighbor.","Assuming P-delta effects are automatically accounted for. If story drift exceeds 0.02H, P-delta analysis is required because second-order effects become significant."]} />
